newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker after afternoon decline.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker after afternoon decline.

text.p: An afternoon selloff took Kuala Lumpur share prices to a lower finish after another thinly-traded session.

"It's just a lack of participation in the market," said an institutional dealer with a bank-linked brokerage firm. "There was selective buying interest in some stocks on the Second Board like Bescorp. But it's more or less unchanged."
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended off 1.94 points to 1,191.89, while the Second Board index slipped 2.10 points to 527.91 after rising as high as 533.88 earlier.
A sharp drop in Japan's Nikkei index led a generally downcast Asian bourse performance, said another institutional dealer. The Nikkei shed 320.43 points to 20,093.03.
"I think that's why principally there was regional weakness," the dealer said.
Dealers said news of a 3.3 percent rise in the Malaysian Consumer Price Index for November had little market impact. "There's nothing surprising," a dealer said.
At the close, over 126 million shares had traded, compared with 118 million on Tuesday. Losers outpaced gainers by 355 to 185.
